speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's going on, can you tell me how long you've had these skin lesions and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the daycare exposure and the brother's recent chickenpox, I suspect Molluscum contagiosum. Do the papules have a central dimple or umbilication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you, that central umbilication is a classic sign of Molluscum contagiosum. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out any secondary bacterial infection, I will request a clinical examination of the lesions. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Exam
